text.p: These are the leading stories in the Namibian press on Monday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The government has ordered the Kxoe community to vacate community-based tourism camps in the West Caprivi. At least four Kxoe community tourism sites and a hunting camp will be hit by the move. The Kxoe will be moved from land they see as traditionally theirs, and which has been regarded as an official nature conservation area, to make way for the expansion of a prison.

- Namibian police caught a Windhoek buisnessman in the possession of two elephant tusks worth N$60,000. The incident occurs on the eve of the CITES conference in Harare on proposing a limited trade in ivory.

- Air Namibia has admitted serious financial losses for the second time in less than a month and has also announced that the possibility of buying a new passenger plane worth N$500 million is being investigated. The airline has also reiterated its plans to go into a strategic partnership with an international airline.
